title: Evaluating LLMs as Agentic Workflow Executors in Real-World Customer Support Skills
abstract: arXiv:2610.14346v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Enterprise customer-support agents increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) to execute bounded, tool-using workflows. We study this problem through the lens of Skill LLMs: specialized executors that operate within a selected skill context and must complete a narrow, stateful workflow under policy and tool constraints. We present a benchmark construction pipeline that mines recurrent workflows from real-world transcripts, converts them into structured skill descriptions, maps them to tool requirements, simulates environment state with Model Context Protocol (MCP)-compatible mocks, and generates multi-turn tool-using dialogues. translated_title: 评估大语言模型作为真实世界客户支持技能中的智能体工作流执行器
translated_abstract: 企业客户支持智能体日益依赖大语言模型（LLM）来执行有界的、使用工具的工作流。我们通过“技能大语言模型”（Skill LLM）的视角研究这一问题：这类专用执行器在选定的技能上下文中运行，必须在策略和工具的约束下完成范围狭窄的、有状态的工作流。我们提出了一个基准构建流程，该流程从真实世界的对话记录中挖掘重复出现的工作流，将其转换为结构化的技能描述，映射到工具需求，使用与模型上下文协议（MCP）兼容的模拟工具来模拟环境状态，并生成多轮次使用工具的对话。基于该基准，我们对17个语言模型进行了大规模零样本评估，涵盖闭源模型系列以及参数量从1.7B到14B的面向部署的开源权重模型，每个模型由五个强大的LLM评审员独立评判，此外还有一个确定性的基于规则的评估器来检查工具调用行为。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个从真实客户支持对话记录中挖掘并构建的基准，用于评估大语言模型在策略与工具约束下执行有状态的多轮工具调用工作流的能力，并对17个闭源与开源模型进行了大规模零样本评测。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a benchmark construction pipeline mined from real-world customer support transcripts to evaluate LLMs as specialized executors of narrow, stateful, tool-constrained workflows, with a large-scale zero-shot evaluation of 17 closed and open-weight models.
